newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ANAHEIM BEATS DETROIT FOR FIRST TIME EVER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-ANAHEIM BEATS DETROIT FOR FIRST TIME EVER.

text.p: Guy Hebert made 31 saves and Garry Valk's second-period goal snapped a tie as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim posted their first-ever victory over the Detroit Red Wings, 3-1 on Sunday.
Teemu Selanne and Darren Van Impe scored the other goals for the Mighty Ducks, who had been 0-9-3 against the Red Wings.
"We were aggressive tonight, not passive," said Anaheim coach Ron Wilson.
Anaheim improved to 3-2-1 in their last six games, while Hebert, coming off his first shutout of the season on Saturday, improved to 3-8-4.

The go-ahead goal came with 9:29 left in the second. Ted Drury had the puck in the left corner before passing to Valk in the slot. Valk put a wrist shot through the pads of goaltender Mike Vernon as he was being pulled down.

Nicklas Lidstrom had the only goal for Detroit, which went 2-1-1 on its four-game road trip and lost for just the second time in its last eight games, 5-2-1. The Red Wings were 4-0-2 in six previous trips to Anaheim.

After a scoreless first period, Steve Yzerman had the puck behind the Anaheim net and flipped a pass to Lidstrom, who batted it out of the air and into the top right corner at 6:33 of the second. It was Lidstrom's fourth goal of the season and third in as many games.
"We came off a big win last night so we felt real good," Hebert said. "We were a little tired but they played last night too. I think this was a great effort by our guys tonight."
Selanne's 13th goal tied the score 1-1 with 9:51 left in the second. Paul Kariya passed to Selanne, who broke into the Detroit zone alone before snapping a wirst shot between Vernon's pads.
Van Impe beat Vernon with a slap shot from the top of the left faceoff circle with 1:46 left in the third period for his first goal since April 4 to complete the scoring..
Vernon made 20 saves and had his personal three-game winning streak snapped.
